subject: Discovery recap: SDK onboarding & request-id strategy
messages:

Subject: Discovery recap: SDK onboarding & request-id strategy

Hi Samir / Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so your engineering team can start scoping integration work. TL;DR: SDK install + auth, routing model variants, structured output/tool-calling, embeddings/rerankers, and a clear 429/retry + request-id plan.

Key notes from call:
- Primary use case: in-product assistant for transaction reconciliation (short ctx, high QPS bursts).
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for text generation path; embeddings acceptable at ~500ms.
- Traffic profile: baseline 200 rps, spikes to 1.2k rps for 30–90s.
- Data residency: US only; no PII persisted in logs.

Proposed integration checklist (attached as pdf):
1) SDK onboarding
   - Install: npm/redwood SDK + v1.2.0 sample.
   - Auth: short-lived service keys via our KMS integration; rotate every 24h.
2) Routing and model variants
   - Route low-latency prompts to smaller distil model; fall back to higher-quality on longer requests.
3) Structured output/tool calling
   - Use our schema-based output (JSON schema validation on the SDK) for tool-calls.
4) Embeddings and reranker
   - Store vectors in your vector DB; use embed+rerank pair to reduce generation calls.
5) Rate limiting / retries / idempotency
   - Use request-id header for all client calls, with idempotency for state-changing ops.
   - Employ exponential backoff with jitter for 429s/503s.

Open questions for your engineers (please share names and a Slack or email contact):
- Do you have a preferred idempotency storage (Redis/DB) and TTL for ops?
- Are you planning to bundle multiple user events into single calls (batching)?
- Which parts of the request pipeline must be strictly idempotent vs best-effort?

Next steps:
- Marissa to share an internal tech note with recommended retry windows and recommended request-id formats.
- Finova to confirm engineering POC owners and desired go/no-go date (we suggested Aug 20 for a small POC).
- Quick follow-up call next week to align on quotas and dedicated capacity threshold.

Attachments: sdk_onboarding_checklist.pdf, request-id-patterns.md

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: SDK onboarding & request-id strategy

Hi Samir / Alex — quick technical responses below; pasting some recommended defaults so your infra team can evaluate. Feel free to share this directly with your SREs.

Request-ID and routing
- Header: X-Request-Id: UUIDv4 is perfect. Add X-Tenant-Id if you want multi-tenant routing on our side; we don't require it but accept it.
- Purpose: request-id should be generated at ingress and propagated downstream to all retries. It is the primary key for dedup detection in the request window.

Idempotency model
- Redwood supports idempotency keys at the API operation level (you can pass Idempotency-Key header). For hosted customers we keep a short-lived index (configurable, default 10 minutes) to dedupe identical create/update operations. For Private deployments you can point that to your Redis instance via our config.
- Recommended pattern: 1) Use Idempotency-Key for create/update; 2) store the key + response status/response-body-hash; 3) TTL = expected retry window + safety margin (we recommend 10–15 minutes for QPS-burst scenarios).

Retries and 429 handling
- For 429/503: exponential backoff starting at 100ms, factor 2, max backoff 5s, with full jitter. Example: client waits random(0, base * 2^n).
- Client should retry only idempotent operations automatically. Non-idempotent operations must surface retryable error to calling code and return a clear retry-after header if possible.
- When possible use our SDK's built-in retry middleware which injects the request-id and handles backoff/jitter.

Embeddings / reranker guidance
- Embeddings: recommend client-side caching for hot id vectors (TTL ~24h) plus server-side prefix caching at the Redwood runtime to avoid repeated inference for the same inputs.
- Reranker: run rerank locally where possible (scores only) and call generation only for top-k results. This reduces generation QPS and improves cost.

Routing & quotas
- Route-based quotas supported: you can configure model-route per API key and set per-route qps and per-project burst caps. During spikes lower-priority routes get rate-limited first, with options to degrade quality (switch to smaller model) instead of outright reject.

I'll drop a short note doc (request-id-patterns.md) with example headers, pseudocode for retry/backoff, and our recommended Redis schema for idempotency.

Cheers,
